excerpt: Vokal is a shared workspace where a team and its Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Hermes agents work in the same channels. $20 per human seat; agents free.
content:
Vokal is a team workspace for companies that already hand work to AI coding and research agents. Instead of each person running Claude Code or Codex in a private terminal and pasting results around, the agents join shared channels as named teammates, each with a role, an owner, its own memory and its own permissions. Anyone in a thread can redirect an agent with an @mention, the owner sees every step and can stop it, and emails or app actions can wait as drafts until a person sends them.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Hermes Agent, running on your own computer or in Vokal Cloud, which the company says is rolling out by workspace. The agents use the AI subscriptions your team already pays for, and Vokal says it never bills for model usage. Agents can act in GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion, Gmail and other apps you connect, with access set per agent. There are desktop apps for Mac and Windows and an iPhone app; the website handles sign-up and billing, and there is no full web version of the workspace.

Pricing is $20 per active human seat per workspace per month, with a 7-day trial that needs no payment method. Vokal was founded by Zhen Han, who says he previously worked at Meta and Google, with co-founder Kai Sun. It launched on Product Hunt on 2 June 2026, hunted by Chris Messina, and finished #2 for the day with 430 upvotes and 54 comments.

We have not tested Vokal ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing and privacy pages, its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

alternatives.intro: Vokal compares itself with Slack's agent features and with Paperclip on its own site. Prices come from each product's own page, checked on 14 October 2026.

quotes.text: for engineers, why is it better than a well set repository with skills, subagents, or other assisting markdowns?
quotes.reply: Repo context helps an agent work inside the codebase; Vokal covers the layer around it: why the work is being done, who asked, what the agent did and who reviewed it.
quotes.author: Artem Litvinenko

quotes.text: How does Vokal handle permissions when one agent needs context from another teammate's workflow?
quotes.reply: Shared context does not mean blanket access. An agent works from channels it belongs to and apps it has been granted; private context has to be brought into a shared thread or granted.
quotes.author: Ada Johnsen

faq.a: A workspace where a team and the AI agents it already uses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Hermes Agent) work together in shared channels. Each agent has a name, a role, an owner, its own memory and permissions, and people decide what ships.
$20 per active human seat per workspace per month, with a 7-day trial and no payment method needed to start. Agents never take a seat. Larger teams can ask for a Custom Package.

faq.q: Do I need a new AI subscription?
faq.a: No. Vokal says agents run on your team's existing AI subscriptions and it never bills for model usage. You still pay your AI provider for those subscriptions.

faq.q: Which devices does it run on?
faq.a: Mac, Windows and iPhone. Voice huddles with agents are on desktop. The website handles sign-up, billing and pairing a phone; there is no full web version.

faq.q: How does Vokal keep agents in check?
faq.a: Each agent has an owner and its own permissions. Local agents can be limited to folders you choose, app access is set per agent, some actions wait as drafts, and the owner can stop an agent at any step.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Vokal?
faq.a: Slack with its AI and partner agents, or Paperclip, an open-source system for running a team of agents. Vokal's difference is that agents join as owned teammates on your own subscriptions.

paragraphs: Zhen Han says AI agents have made individual builders much faster, but software is still built by teams. One person uses ChatGPT, another Claude Code or Codex in a terminal, another Cursor, and the prompts, decisions and follow-ups travel between them by copy and paste.

Vokal is his answer: one workspace where people and agents share the goal, the right agent is assigned, everyone can watch and review the work in context, and useful outputs are saved for the next run. Each agent gets a name, role, owner, permissions, app access and memory scope, whether it runs locally or in the cloud.
